title: Scam or fine?
instruction: You got these messages and offers on social media. Which are scams?

items.text: You’ve won; pay €2 postage within 24 hours
items.why: You never pay for a real prize, and certainly not in a hurry.

items.text: A competition on a cinema’s verified profile: write in the comments which film you would go to
items.why: It wants nothing from you, and the organiser is real.

items.text: A friend: send me the code you just got, I put in your number by mistake
items.why: The code is the key to your account. And her account has most likely been stolen.

items.text: A well-known YouTuber in a video: send me €20 and I’ll send you back 40
items.why: A deepfake with a promise to double your money.

items.text: A shop shows you a discount code in its official app
items.why: A discount right in the shop’s app; you enter nothing.

items.text: A profile with a bank’s name: verify your account or it will be blocked
items.why: Fear and hurry. Your bank will contact you in the bank’s app, not on social media.

debrief: A scam gives itself away by what it wants: money, your card, a password or a code, and right now. A real competition and a real friend need none of these.
